resources.string: Tips are on the Play Store version

Quick start
 1. Install Torque Pro (the paid version; Torque Lite does not support plugins) and pair your OBD-II adapter.
 2. Enable this plugin in Torque → Settings → Plugins.
 3. Allow notifications, and set battery use to Unrestricted so Torque can start this plugin in the background.
 4. In Torque, select the vehicle profile for the car you are driving. Data is kept per Torque profile.
 5. Choose the Fuel source below. Tank size is only the current guess; it is updated at fills and when Torque disconnects.
 6. In Torque, add gauges for [FuelSmooth] Smoothed Fuel Level, Corrected Fuel Level and Fuel Remaining.
 7. With Feed fuel level back to Torque (overrides 012F) on, your existing 012F fuel gauge shows the chosen value.
 8. Drive normally. The plugin runs only while Torque is connected to the ECU.
 9. Keep driving and filling up. Corrected % and fuel remaining get accurate over several partial tanks.
 10. If a Wrong vehicle profile? notification appears, choose what to do with that drive.
Feed fuel level back to Torque (overrides 012F)
Battery/background start was denied. Open once so the plugin can run with Torque.

Add additional tanks as needed (stock tank 1 always stays). Do not switch senders onto the PCM FLI pin (false fill). Each extra tank needs its own Torque extra PID (MCU Mode 22, unique name — not 012F or Ford 16C1). Select-PID value is the 1-based tank id. Gal/hr is charged only to the active tank.
